bounded_question: How does TableCache consult the fragmented range tombstones when serving a Get and when refreshing cached seqnums?

update_range_tombstone_seqnums.role: For each level in [struct+0x08, struct+0x10) whose bit is CLEAR in the combined mask (struct+0x18 | struct+0x20 | base+0xf08), raise the cached max covering seqnum and refresh the covering-key string.

level_loop.skip_rule: bit SET in the combined mask -> skip

tablecache_get.role: Point lookup: consult the range tombstones first (when gated in), then perform the table Get via vtable slot 0x58. This packet pins the tombstone consultation; the value lookup itself is cited by contract.

gate_order.on_true: release iterator via slot 0x8, then the table Get (0x5f40199)

user_key_slice.note: built on the stack from the internal key: ptr = *(rcx), len = *(rcx+8) - 8 (the 8-byte seqnum/type trailer is stripped)

table_get.role: the table reader's Get (cited by contract)

get_fallback_null_reader.role: Get helper used when the reader is null (cited by contract)

get_tail_marker.role: writes +0x108 = 1 and clears the byte at *(+0x1a0) when the status code is 7 and *(rcx+0x28) == 1 (cited by contract)

not_ready_path.role: lookup helpers used when the file is not yet opened (cited by contract)

get_cleanup_fragment.role: Exception-cleanup fragment FDE for Get: the landing pads at 0x5f40a69/0x5f40a75/0x5f40a81 jump here (0x5f40027/0x5f4000e/0x5f4001b).

shared_update.rule: Let m = MaxCoveringTombstoneSeqnum(iterator, key). If m <= *cached_max, change nothing. Else store m into *cached_max; when the +0x190 string slot is non-null, replace the string with the key-array Slice at the returned seqnum's index; set +0x198 = 1.
shared_update.fragment_index_arithmetic: index = (seq_ptr - seq_base) >> 3; entry = the 16-byte Slice at key_base + index * 16. In the binary: (rax - *(rdx+0x18)) >> 3 << 4 + *(rdx+0x30), where rdx = iterator+0x68 (the list) and rax = iterator+0x90 (the seq pointer).

null_stub.meaning: the null-returning default for the slot-0x18 iterator build: a reader with this slot has no range tombstones to consult

iterator_gate_memtable.role: MemTable-side iterator gate (cited; #3674/#3900 ground): return null when the +0x35 byte of the second argument is nonzero, or when the MemTable's +0xa60 byte is nonzero; else tail-jump to NewRangeTombstoneIteratorInternal 0x5f0a9c0. The +0x35 test is the same offset the Get gate tests.

callee_contract.contract: SeekToCoveringTombstone; Valid check; return 0 when invalid, when seq_ptr == fragment range end, or when the fragment start key is greater than the key; else return *(+0x90).

cache_chain_canonicals.note: Get's cleanup regions walk +0x38 chains comparing vtable slots 0x18/0x38/0x40 against GOT canonicals (8 levels unrolled, then a virtual call). The canonicals resolve to cache-wrapper vtable slots; the chain resolution itself is cited by contract.

literals.role: guard byte for the lazy static at 0x65046a0 (the +0x38-chain object in Get)

cited_only.role: Get helper when the reader is null; 10 call sites
0x20-byte deleter for the lazy static at 0x65046a0
sole caller of UpdateRangeTombstoneSeqnums (site 0x5f44279); a 5001-byte multi-level lookup; its level-range struct is filled at 0x5f4308f/0x5f4309d
sole caller of TableCache::Get (site 0x5f738e8); passes the per-file record (index*0x3c8) and the +0x1118 struct as stack arguments

unknowns: The C++ names of the two hosts (described by behaviour).
The semantic identity of the key-array Slice refreshed into +0x190 (fragment start key vs end key vs timestamp key) — carried open from #3900.
The exact roles of the three mask words in the refresh loop (struct+0x18, struct+0x20, base+0xf08) beyond the observed skip rule.
The class behind the slot-0x18 receiver in each host (the vtable is not named; only the canonical guard is pinned).
The identity of the +0x35 flag's owner struct (the same offset is tested by the MemTable gate 0x5f0b050 and by Get; likely a ReadOptions field, not proven here).

The full value-lookup behaviour of TableCache::Get beyond the tombstone consultation (slot-0x58 table Get, the +0x38/+0x40 cache chain-walks, the 0x5f3f6c0 fallback and the not-ready path are cited, not modelled).
The landing-pad / LSDA tables of both hosts.

census.method: one objdump pass over the executable LOAD segment, direct call/jump/lea census plus 8-byte qword scan and RELATIVE relocations; see census.py
